Research & Engineering Lineage

SSS-L1 — Software Architecture

This account explains the historical public 68-property study at immutable custody commit cacfe97da7656b472bf4f11e50c9d106a6c3f92a. The separately accepted current r1 subject has its own exact identity and interpretation. Historical 68-row coverage is not a claim to publish that protected successor explanation. Family · Genealogy · All 68 historical properties · Current metadata.

What the lineage studies

Software Architecture concerns consequential software organisation, interaction, decisions and qualities. The historical study distinguishes the system's architecture, its description and beliefs about it. A clear diagram can describe an unsuitable design; a description standard organises an account without certifying the described system. The relevant question is which relationships matter to an actual concern and how a proposed choice changes an observable consequence. Historical public intake.

Its plural genealogy connects abstraction and information hiding, program families and reuse, conceptual integrity, component/connector styles, multiple views, formal architectural languages, scenario evaluation, decision knowledge, conformance and revision. The analytical label “Evolved Software Architecture” names this study's reconstruction; it is not an invented academic school or a claim of consensus. The source table retains exact works, editions, inspected locators and access limits. Historical source table.

Predicates that survive the history

Information hiding ties a boundary to design decisions expected to change. The useful outcome is protection of relevant client obligations, not the largest possible component count. A uses relation is not simply a procedure-call relation. Interface assumptions include meaning and interaction, so matching signatures or separate deployments can coexist with architectural mismatch. A direct call, ordinary module or modular monolith can remain the appropriate alternative when distribution supplies no needed independence. Historical properties ESA-007, ESA-008 and ESA-010.

A quality label becomes assessable through a scenario and an observable response. A tactic needs a plausible mechanism, and an apparent benefit must respect other constraints and measurement boundaries. Risk workshops can expose assumptions and tradeoffs without predicting every operating condition. The historical comparative evidence is limited and context-specific; it does not establish one universally superior evaluation method. Historical public intake, quality reasoning.

Views, decision records and conformance checks earn their place through a consumer. Kruchten's 4+1 approach permits unnecessary views to be omitted. A concise rationale can preserve knowledge, but a completed record does not show that its decision is sound or current. A mapped conformance discrepancy can reveal an implementation problem or an obsolete baseline; restoration of the old rule is not automatically the right action. Historical source records ESA-S003, ESA-S027/029 and ESA-S045.

Concrete discriminators and alternatives

Reusable components can bring incompatible assumptions about their environment or interaction. Their individual success does not settle the assembled system. A purportedly isolated service can still share capacity or state. The appropriate inquiry follows the relevant interaction and failure containment; it does not assume isolation from a box boundary. The historical mismatch case and deployment accounts support this distinction at their own scopes. Historical public intake.

Formal connector analysis has a model-relative guarantee under its stated well-formedness and compatibility premises. Compatibility alone is insufficient. The implementation and environmental correspondence must survive before the result is used to support a realised claim. A model's continued validity need not be denied when the unsupported part is its application. Runtime adaptation adds observation, model, permitted action, actual execution and observed consequence; a functioning loop or improved local score is not the whole obligation. Historical formal and adaptation source partitions.

The smallest coherent form can be a short discussion, an explicit constraint, a local choice and a focused check. Richer models, workshops and records can be economical under difficult coordination, turnover or high consequences. They are conditional instruments. One mechanism can serve several concerns, and one property row does not imply a new owner, document or control. Historical composition model.

Criticism, adverse findings and evidence limits

The historical study rejects architecture-by-artifact, universal central approval, obligatory complete view sets, maximal service decomposition, a review as an operating-quality certificate, smell scores as architectural truth and all deviations as harmful erosion. It also distinguishes organisational association from deterministic causation. The constructive response is proportionate reasoning with a consumer, consequence and condition for revisiting or retiring the mechanism. Historical public intake, caricatures and ceremonies.

The 68 historical candidates include favorable, conditional, rejected, ceremonial, non-general, superseded and unresolved records. All remain in the complete reader. The 66 historical source records are not 66 independent experiments. Formal results, historical arguments, small task comparisons, field accounts, reused datasets and partially accessed works support different claims. Autonomous architecting remains an unresolved historical capability claim, rather than either an established practice or proof of impossibility. Later current corrections and qualification are separate. Historical ledger · Current identity registry.

Existing receiving responsibility

The repository's R003C qualification gives an already-public complete-member and selected-consumer account for #228. Full disposition is not full operative absorption or acceptance of all SSS. The Architecture rough outline routes later exact-current questions to existing owners and allows no change. It does not reopen or close an issue.

SSS family · Software Maintenance and Evolution · Software Product Line Engineering

Lineage class:

ANALYTICAL_CRITICISM_OF_ARCHITECTURAL_PRACTICE

Original form:

The shorthand that architecture encompasses all important decisions.

Problem it addressed:

The label is used to claim authority over all important engineering or business matters.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

The shorthand is circular when importance is undefined and can annex detailed design, governance or enterprise strategy.

Lineage class:

NATIVE_SOFTWARE_ARCHITECTURE_OR_DOCUMENTED_INTERNAL_EXTENSION

Original form:

Allocate module responsibilities around design decisions expected to change rather than processing steps.

Problem it addressed:

A likely change currently propagates through clients that need only the stable service or invariant.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: The selected change can be made without corresponding changes in clients that should be insulated.

Mechanism:

Place knowledge of a plausibly varying design decision behind an interface whose clients need not depend on that decision; separate stable obligations from hidden choices.

Trigger or context:

A likely change currently propagates through clients that need only the stable service or invariant.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Keep a straightforward local implementation where the variation is unlikely or the extra boundary costs more than the expected change.

Dependencies or preconditions:

A defensible change hypothesis and an interface that can express required behaviour without leaking the hidden choice.

Domain profile:

Architectural object and abstraction level

Module responsibilities and design-knowledge boundaries, not deployment units.

Stakeholders and concerns

Module designers and dependent implementers/maintainers. The concern is activated by: A likely change currently propagates through clients that need only the stable service or invariant.

Quality scenario and response measure

Try a representative change and observe affected obligations and components; do not equate module count with modifiability.

Structural or behavioural mechanism

Place knowledge of a plausibly varying design decision behind an interface whose clients need not depend on that decision; separate stable obligations from hidden choices.

Interface and dependency assumptions

A defensible change hypothesis and an interface that can express required behaviour without leaking the hidden choice.

Parnas 1972 change-oriented responsibility allocation, extended through family design. Current reopening rule: Reopen the boundary when the actual change pattern or performance needs contradict its original rationale.

Lineage class:

NATIVE_SOFTWARE_ARCHITECTURE_OR_DOCUMENTED_INTERNAL_EXTENSION

Original form:

Components and connectors describe computation and interaction rather than an untyped boxes-and-arrows picture.

Problem it addressed:

Interaction semantics affect coupling, performance, consistency, failure handling or allowed composition.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: Consumers can explain what an interaction does and which participant or shared resource controls it.

Mechanism:

Model or inspect the actual interaction mechanism—call, event, stream, shared store or protocol—and its control/data consequences instead of treating an arrow as self-explanatory.

Trigger or context:

Interaction semantics affect coupling, performance, consistency, failure handling or allowed composition.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Name and test a simple direct call; do not create a connector abstraction or framework when ordinary language captures the needed semantics.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Knowledge of communication direction, synchrony, state and failure behaviour.

Domain profile:

Architectural object and abstraction level

Runtime and logical interaction relations, at the level required by the concern.

Stakeholders and concerns

Component authors, protocol designers and integration/operations staff. The concern is activated by: Interaction semantics affect coupling, performance, consistency, failure handling or allowed composition.

Quality scenario and response measure

Test the selected interaction’s response, blocking and failure properties rather than count arrows.

Structural or behavioural mechanism

Model or inspect the actual interaction mechanism—call, event, stream, shared store or protocol—and its control/data consequences instead of treating an arrow as self-explanatory.

Interface and dependency assumptions

Knowledge of communication direction, synchrony, state and failure behaviour.

Description implementation correspondence

The architectural assertion must be checked at the declared object/observation scope. Evidence sought: Consumers can explain what an interaction does and which participant or shared resource controls it. Validity boundary: Reifying every connector adds machinery; an explicitly drawn connector can still hide transport, state or callback assumptions.

Decision rationale and reopening condition

Component-and-connector architecture treats interaction as a first-class design subject. Current reopening rule: Reopen when transport, synchrony, multiplicity or shared-resource behaviour changes.

Change propagation or evolution consequence

The controlled consequence is: Consumers can explain what an interaction does and which participant or shared resource controls it. Reconsider the mechanism when its expected effect changes: Reopen when transport, synchrony, multiplicity or shared-resource behaviour changes.

Evaluation method and validity limit

Test the selected interaction’s response, blocking and failure properties rather than count arrows. Reifying every connector adds machinery; an explicitly drawn connector can still hide transport, state or callback assumptions.

Coordination cost and minimal alternative

Name and test a simple direct call; do not create a connector abstraction or framework when ordinary language captures the needed semantics. Fuller work is justified by: Interaction semantics affect coupling, performance, consistency, failure handling or allowed composition.

Expected engineering payoff:

Claim

Consumers can explain what an interaction does and which participant or shared resource controls it.

Evidence boundary

A defensible intended consequence, not a measured universal effect; evidence partitions below constrain the claim.

Decision or consumer:

Component authors, protocol designers and integration/operations staff.

Actor and authority boundary:

Component authors, protocol designers and integration/operations staff. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.

Communication or interaction requirement:

Producer and consumer exchange the obligations and hidden assumptions that affect composition; communicate changed semantics, not merely changed signatures. Specific subject: Connectors as explicit interaction mechanisms.

Observable postcondition:

Consumers can explain what an interaction does and which participant or shared resource controls it.

Known failure modes:

  • Reifying every connector adds machinery; an explicitly drawn connector can still hide transport, state or callback assumptions.

Important criticisms:

Objection

Reifying every connector adds machinery; an explicitly drawn connector can still hide transport, state or callback assumptions.

Do not claim independence where it is unnecessary; a coordinated shared unit can be the simpler honest design.

Original form:

Stakeholders generate and prioritise representative quality concerns and scenarios.

Problem it addressed:

An evaluation or design claim depends on a selected set of scenarios.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: The conclusion states the population to which scenarios apply and the consequential conditions not covered.

Mechanism:

Examine which users, operating states, changes and adverse cases the scenario set represents; add decision-changing omissions and preserve uncertainty rather than treating prioritisation as completeness.

Trigger or context:

An evaluation or design claim depends on a selected set of scenarios.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Use a few explicit favourable, adverse and boundary cases for a small decision, with limits stated; avoid exhaustive catalogues with no consumer.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Knowledge of relevant stakeholders and operating variation plus a means to challenge the initial scenario selection.

Domain profile:

Architectural object and abstraction level

Scenario population, sampling and prioritisation at evaluation scope.

Stakeholders and concerns

Evaluators and affected participants, including dissenting or absent-user representatives where warranted. The concern is activated by: An evaluation or design claim depends on a selected set of scenarios.

Quality scenario and response measure

Coverage is judged against the decision’s concern population; number of scenarios alone does not establish representativeness.

Structural or behavioural mechanism

Examine which users, operating states, changes and adverse cases the scenario set represents; add decision-changing omissions and preserve uncertainty rather than treating prioritisation as completeness.

Interface and dependency assumptions

Knowledge of relevant stakeholders and operating variation plus a means to challenge the initial scenario selection.

Evidence sought: The conclusion states the population to which scenarios apply and the consequential conditions not covered. Scenario methods require selection; critiques of coverage arise from omissions and limited evaluation populations. Current reopening rule: Reopen when a new user, failure, workload or change pattern could reverse the decision.

Connect a tactic to the model parameters it changes and to the response sought; account for interactions, overhead and assumptions that make the causal explanation plausible.

One representation obscures materially different structural, runtime, deployment or development questions.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Mechanism:

Select viewpoints by the concerns and decisions they enable, then create only the views needed to communicate or analyse those concerns.

Trigger or context:

A recurring architectural problem matches the style’s assumptions closely enough to reduce design or analysis effort.

Failure to secure this consequence: The adopted structure exhibits the relevant mechanism and satisfies its selected concerns under stated assumptions.

Use a style or pattern as a conditional mechanism with an explicit problem, constraints and trade-offs; document purposeful hybrids and their interaction obligations.

Trigger or context:

A recurring architectural problem matches the style’s assumptions closely enough to reduce design or analysis effort.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Use a direct design without a pattern label when the pattern adds indirection or excludes a better local arrangement.

Understanding of the style’s actual semantics, not only its name; compatibility of combined mechanisms.

Test the style’s claimed response and imposed costs in the target scenario; adoption frequency is not effectiveness.

Modifiability or the consequences of planned change are material and can be expressed as concrete scenarios.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: The evaluation reveals where changes propagate and where multiple changes depend on the same structural decision.

Mechanism:

Walk representative modifications through an architecture, identify affected elements and interacting scenarios, and compare the resulting burdens across alternatives.

Trigger or context:

Modifiability or the consequences of planned change are material and can be expressed as concrete scenarios.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Walk a single realistic change through the current code and a proposed alternative if a full workshop is unnecessary.

Architecture knowledge, credible change scenarios and estimates grounded in how modifications would actually be made.

Architectural object and abstraction level

Architecture under prospective functional or quality-related modifications.

Quality scenario and response measure

Compare explained change impact and, when available, actual later change work; do not equate workshop completion with prediction accuracy.

Structural or behavioural mechanism

Walk representative modifications through an architecture, identify affected elements and interacting scenarios, and compare the resulting burdens across alternatives.

Interface and dependency assumptions

Architecture knowledge, credible change scenarios and estimates grounded in how modifications would actually be made.

Original form:

The ceremony of treating document volume or template completion as evidence of quality.

Problem it addressed:

Page counts, completed templates or a large repository of records are used as assurance.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Fragments, obsolete rationale and conflicting copies can make extensive documentation worse than a concise current account.

Mechanism:

Document quantity alone is not retained as a proxy for architectural knowledge, correctness or maintenance value.

Trigger or context:

Page counts, completed templates or a large repository of records are used as assurance.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Ask a real consumer to recover a needed decision or check a correspondence using the smallest adequate material.

Dependencies or preconditions:

A useful documentation intervention requires a consumer, question and maintained link to the relevant system.

Domain profile:

Architectural object and abstraction level

Documentation volume as a candidate architectural quality indicator.

Stakeholders and concerns

Use a smell or detector output to prioritise investigation, then connect it to actual quality, invariant or change burden before prescribing repair.

There are enough suspected structural problems that triage may save investigation effort.

Investigate a concrete recurring failure directly; skip a detector when its noise costs more than manual diagnosis.

Defined detector semantics, calibration/known errors and a link between the indicator and the concern of interest.

Potential architectural risk indicators extracted from code, graphs or review text.

Use target-specific precision/recall and measured consequences where feasible; score reduction alone is not remediation value.

Original form:

An architectural model mediates observation, adaptation decisions and changes to a running system.

Problem it addressed:

Operating variation warrants runtime reconfiguration and appropriate actions are available.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: The requested adaptation is actually enacted and subsequent observations show its bounded consequence.

Mechanism:

Observe the running system, interpret observations in an architecture model, choose among allowed changes and execute them through available effectors; keep system-specific translation explicit.

Trigger or context:

Operating variation warrants runtime reconfiguration and appropriate actions are available.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Use a stable configuration, an operator procedure or a simple established controller when architecture-level adaptation adds no value.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Observable state, timely valid sensors/model, specified strategies and effectors capable of making the intended changes.

Architectural object and abstraction level

Runtime architectural configurations, monitors, model and control actions.

Stakeholders and concerns

Runtime controllers within delegated limits, with engineers/operators responsible for those limits and failures. The concern is activated by: Operating variation warrants runtime reconfiguration and appropriate actions are available.

Observe model freshness, action completion and post-change qualities under the stated operating envelope.

Structural or behavioural mechanism

Observe the running system, interpret observations in an architecture model, choose among allowed changes and execute them through available effectors; keep system-specific translation explicit.

Invest in flexibility when a credible change family and its expected cost justify the present complexity; preserve simpler reversible choices where evidence is weak.

Lineage class:

NATIVE_SOFTWARE_ARCHITECTURE_OR_DOCUMENTED_INTERNAL_EXTENSION

Original form:

A single deployable system can have deliberate internal modules; consolidation can remove needless service coordination.

Problem it addressed:

Shared release, scale, trust or operations make independent deployment unnecessary or harmful.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: The system retains required modular reasoning while removing unneeded distributed coordination.

Mechanism:

Preserve useful logical boundaries inside a shared deployment, or consolidate services whose separation adds costs without a needed independent capability.

Trigger or context:

Learned components influence consequential system outputs or are reused by downstream consumers.

Include training/serving data, model behaviour, undeclared consumers and feedback paths in architectural reasoning; treat distribution and model changes as potential contract changes.

Learned components influence consequential system outputs or are reused by downstream consumers.

DOCUMENTED_IMPORT_OF_LLM_ASSISTANCE

Original form:

LLMs assist decision generation, architecture evaluation and pattern selection.

Problem it addressed:

AI assistance could reduce search/drafting effort and adequate validation is available.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: Accepted AI-assisted claims have an independent basis and unsupported material remains labelled or rejected.

Mechanism:

Use generated alternatives, descriptions or risk suggestions as candidates; independently check their evidence, semantics, metrics and fit to the actual system before relying on them.

Trigger or context:

AI assistance could reduce search/drafting effort and adequate validation is available.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Use direct human analysis, deterministic extraction or established checks when verification costs exceed the assistance benefit.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Accessible underlying evidence, explicit task scope, recorded model/prompt context and an evaluator not simply reusing the generated claim as its oracle.

Domain profile:

Architectural object and abstraction level

AI-produced architectural representations, options, risk analyses and boundary proposals.

Stakeholders and concerns

Human or otherwise authorised reviewers who retain decision responsibility; generated text has no operative mandate. The concern is activated by: AI assistance could reduce search/drafting effort and adequate validation is available.

Quality scenario and response measure

Compare externally checked correctness and total effort including verification, not model confidence or self-reported quality.

Structural or behavioural mechanism

Use generated alternatives, descriptions or risk suggestions as candidates; independently check their evidence, semantics, metrics and fit to the actual system before relying on them.

Lineage class:

DOCUMENTED_INTERSECTION_WITH_SUSTAINABILITY

Original form:

Architecture choices contribute to energy/resource consequences alongside other quality constraints.

Problem it addressed:

Energy, emissions, resource use or longer-term maintainability are material stakeholder concerns.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: A claimed improvement is tied to the measured concern and boundary, with omitted lifecycle or social effects stated.

Mechanism:

Declare the sustainability concern and system/lifecycle boundary, then evaluate architectural alternatives against measurable impacts and competing constraints rather than assuming a fashionable deployment is greener.

Trigger or context:

Energy, emissions, resource use or longer-term maintainability are material stakeholder concerns.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Use a targeted operational measurement or omit a specialised control when its impact is negligible and its own cost dominates.

Dependencies or preconditions:

An appropriate measurement/accounting boundary, relevant workload and explicit treatment of externalised impacts.

Domain profile:

Architectural object and abstraction level

Architectural choices affecting operational and lifecycle resource consequences.

Stakeholders and concerns

Stakeholders setting impact priorities and engineers able to measure and alter relevant mechanisms. The concern is activated by: Energy, emissions, resource use or longer-term maintainability are material stakeholder concerns.

Quality scenario and response measure

Use the actual chosen impact measure plus performance/availability constraints; do not extrapolate a benchmark saving to whole-system sustainability.

Structural or behavioural mechanism

Declare the sustainability concern and system/lifecycle boundary, then evaluate architectural alternatives against measurable impacts and competing constraints rather than assuming a fashionable deployment is greener.

Interface and dependency assumptions

An appropriate measurement/accounting boundary, relevant workload and explicit treatment of externalised impacts.

Evidence sought: A claimed improvement is tied to the measured concern and boundary, with omitted lifecycle or social effects stated. Validity boundary: Energy is not carbon, package energy is not facility/lifecycle impact and efficiency can induce greater use; the latter is an analytical transfer concern here.

Sustainability research broadens architectural concern selection; energy-aware systems provide bounded interventions. Current reopening rule: Reopen when workload, energy supply, lifecycle scope or external costs change the impact comparison.

NATIVE_SOFTWARE_ARCHITECTURE_OR_DOCUMENTED_INTERNAL_EXTENSION

Original form:

Use architectural work whose benefits justify its coordination, learning and maintenance costs.

Problem it addressed:

Architecture work imposes review, documentation, modelling or coordination cost.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: The retained machinery supports a decision or protects an obligation, and unnecessary machinery can be removed without losing that function.

Mechanism:

Keep only the architectural control, artefact or coordination mechanism whose consumer and avoided risk justify its cost; choose the smallest coherent arrangement and retire obsolete controls.

Architecture work imposes review, documentation, modelling or coordination cost.

The claim that emergent design removes the need for any architectural reasoning.

An evolutionary or agile label is used to avoid considering a consequential interface, quality or migration decision.

Accidental dependencies and irreversible choices arise without explicit plans; conversely excessive anticipation can obstruct learning.

Emergence is not a general exemption from examining architecture-relevant consequences; reason just enough, and revise as the system and knowledge change.

An evolutionary or agile label is used to avoid considering a consequential interface, quality or migration decision.

An Internet-scale distributed-hypermedia interaction problem benefits from visibility, intermediaries and independent evolution.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: The real interactions exhibit the claimed REST constraints and the selected consequences are evaluated.

Mechanism:

Where its context fits, apply REST’s client/server, stateless interaction, cache, uniform-interface and layered constraints together, with optional code-on-demand and their associated trade-offs.

Trigger or context:

An Internet-scale distributed-hypermedia interaction problem benefits from visibility, intermediaries and independent evolution.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Use a simpler local interface or another protocol/style where its constraints impose costs without those benefits; do not call every HTTP API REST.

Actual resource/representation and interaction semantics, cache validity and adherence to the selected style’s constraints.

The SOA reference model relates service description, visibility, interaction, execution context and real-world effect.

Problem it addressed:

A consumer relies on another participant’s capability across a service boundary.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: The consumer can determine whether the intended interaction is possible, allowed and actually produced the relevant effect.

Mechanism:

For a service relationship, distinguish awareness/reachability/willingness, the exchanged information/actions and the consequence that the consumer seeks, including policy or contract conditions.

Trigger or context:

A consumer relies on another participant’s capability across a service boundary.

Non trigger or cheap path:

A direct internal function contract may suffice when there is no separate service/participant relation to manage.

Mutually understood action/information semantics, actual access and applicable conditions; a discoverable endpoint does not establish permission or success.

Providers and consumers within their real policies/contracts; each retains its actual authority boundary. The concern is activated by: A consumer relies on another participant’s capability across a service boundary.

Qualification

Lineage class:

NATIVE_SOFTWARE_ARCHITECTURE_OR_DOCUMENTED_INTERNAL_EXTENSION

Original form:

ADD recursively selects drivers, design concepts, elements, responsibilities and interfaces and checks the result.

Problem it addressed:

A system or element needs deliberate architectural decomposition and the significant drivers are understood sufficiently to guide a choice.

Failure mode it tries to prevent:

Failure to secure this consequence: The chosen decomposition and interfaces can be traced to the drivers, and child obligations are made explicit.

Mechanism:

Use prioritised requirements and constraints to select a consequential element, choose design concepts, allocate responsibilities, define interfaces and refine the resulting obligations; revisit earlier choices when evaluation reveals a problem.

Trigger or context:

A system or element needs deliberate architectural decomposition and the significant drivers are understood sufficiently to guide a choice.

Non trigger or cheap path:

Use a focused local design decision when recursive decomposition would only reproduce the obvious.

Dependencies or preconditions:

Sufficient prioritised drivers, feasible design concepts and ability to evaluate their consequences; requirements need not be complete forever.

Domain profile:

Architectural object and abstraction level

Design of a system or architectural element through requirement allocation and interfaces.

Stakeholders and concerns

Designers and affected stakeholders; algorithmic decomposition does not replace trade-off judgement. The concern is activated by: A system or element needs deliberate architectural decomposition and the significant drivers are understood sufficiently to guide a choice.

Quality scenario and response measure

Evaluate whether the allocated elements can satisfy the selected scenarios and constraints, rather than count completed steps.

Structural or behavioural mechanism

Use prioritised requirements and constraints to select a consequential element, choose design concepts, allocate responsibilities, define interfaces and refine the resulting obligations; revisit earlier choices when evaluation reveals a problem.

Interface and dependency assumptions

Sufficient prioritised drivers, feasible design concepts and ability to evaluate their consequences; requirements need not be complete forever.

Description implementation correspondence

The architectural assertion must be checked at the declared object/observation scope. Evidence sought: The chosen decomposition and interfaces can be traced to the drivers, and child obligations are made explicit. Validity boundary: Recursion can become a paperwork tree or freeze speculative requirements; following eight steps does not validate the chosen design.

Decision rationale and reopening condition

ADD v2.0 turns architectural drivers into recursive element design, allocation and interface refinement. Current reopening rule: Reopen when child-level analysis, prototyping or changed drivers invalidate the parent choice.

Change propagation or evolution consequence

The controlled consequence is: The chosen decomposition and interfaces can be traced to the drivers, and child obligations are made explicit. Reconsider the mechanism when its expected effect changes: Reopen when child-level analysis, prototyping or changed drivers invalidate the parent choice.

Evaluation method and validity limit

Evaluate whether the allocated elements can satisfy the selected scenarios and constraints, rather than count completed steps. Recursion can become a paperwork tree or freeze speculative requirements; following eight steps does not validate the chosen design.

Coordination cost and minimal alternative

Use a focused local design decision when recursive decomposition would only reproduce the obvious. Fuller work is justified by: A system or element needs deliberate architectural decomposition and the significant drivers are understood sufficiently to guide a choice.

Expected engineering payoff:

Claim

The chosen decomposition and interfaces can be traced to the drivers, and child obligations are made explicit.

Evidence boundary

A defensible intended consequence, not a measured universal effect; evidence partitions below constrain the claim.

Decision or consumer:

Designers and affected stakeholders; algorithmic decomposition does not replace trade-off judgement.

Actor and authority boundary:

Designers and affected stakeholders; algorithmic decomposition does not replace trade-off judgement. This criterion does not grant authority, resources or execution capability; those must already exist or be legitimately supplied.

Communication or interaction requirement:

Designers and evaluators exchange alternatives, assumptions and decisive observations; risk identification is not an approval mandate. Specific subject: Driver-based recursive architectural design.

Observable postcondition:

The chosen decomposition and interfaces can be traced to the drivers, and child obligations are made explicit.

  • Recursion can become a paperwork tree or freeze speculative requirements; following eight steps does not validate the chosen design.
